BOOK SIX OF STATIUS' THEBAID

1

The messenger Rumor glides through the Danaan cities with a wide-ranging
step, proclaiming that the Inachidae
1
 are ordering solemn rites
at a new tomb and in addition, an athletic meet, so that they may exercise
and stimulate their martial courage in preparation for war.

1
This term means "the descendants of Inachus" or Argives.
Inachus is the god of the river of the same name in Argos.

The honor of founding the Olympic Games. Legends connected
both Hercules and Pelops with the founding of the games.

Olympic Games. His hair is dusty because of the dust raised by competition
in the stadium.

6
The snake is the Python, which Apollo killed with his bow
and arrow, thereby "freeing" the area for the foundation of the oracle.
This was the event that motivated the foundation of the Pythian Games in
honor of the Python and Apollo at Delphi, which is located in Phocis.

friendly shores at festival time: both shores of the Isthmus cry out with

 Echionian

according to legend, was as part of funeral rites for the child Melicertes,
who was killed when his mother Ino, driven mad by Hera, jumped into the
sea carrying the boy. They both became gods after death. In this new status
Ino was called Leucothea and Melicertes, Palaemon.

or to challenge the Tuscan or the Aegean Sea in winter, first they try

and multiplies the sounds. The father himself, seated, is not wearing

she is eager to prostrate herself on top of the wounded remains of her
son and as often as she is pulled away, comes back. Even her husband himself

 felt their resentment

and with welling tears try to excuse the crime.

The Nemeans resented the Argives because they blamed them

Adrastus himself, as soon as the tumult of the distraught house grew
silent, takes the initiative in consoling the father, now mentioning fate
and the harsh affairs of men and the inexorable spinning of the Fates,

gods, survive.

But before he had a chance to finish, the laments returned. Also the
father listens to this friendly address not more sympathetically than the

the pyre

including Eastern wealth such as lumps of gray incense and cinnamon

the death-bringing dogs:

because it reminded her of her own child's death.

in a funeral procession to the pyre, but empty and sterile glory nevertheless

Immediately the virgin forest, whose foliage had been untouched by the
iron of an ax, is laid low, a forest than which no woods in Argos or Arcadia

by the will of the gods, not only is it said to be older

than human race but also to have witnessed the change of its Nymphs

 The forest suffered a wretched destruction:
wild animals flee, birds fly away from their warm nests, driven by fear;
the high beech tree and the oak grove and the cypress, unharmed by winter,

the pitch-pines lie on the ground, food for funeral fires and so do

because ash trees were used for spear-shafts.

is cut with an odorous wound, the alder, friendly to the sea,

and the elm, hospitable to vines, incline their unshorn crowns to the earth.
The earth moans: not in this way is the forest of Ismarus said to be overturned
when Boreas29 puts forth his head from his broken-open cave, not more quickly
did a nocturnal flame roar through a forest with the aid of the south wind.

White Pales, and Silvanus,

 who presides over the shade

almost immediately after the signal is heard, no city is left; they

when the crooked funereal horn bleated out a low note as a signal for

on which details of a person's career are inscribed. This

Thus she spoke and ceasing her complaints she fell silent. Just as when
a wild beast has taken or a shepherd has led away to the harsh altar a
tottering bullock, which has been cheated out of its first milk and whose
only nourishment is from the teat; the deprived mother rouses now the valley,

Pelops won his bride by defeating her father in a chariot
race. He accomplished this by bribing the father's charioteer, Myrtilus,
to sabotage the chariot. Pelops later murdered Myrtilus by throwing him
from his chariot over a cliff into the sea.

he locked up his daughter Danae in a tower, but Jupiter, taking the form

out to sea in a box. They both survived and later Perseus accidentally
killed Acrisius.

 sons of Belus, join their disharmonious right
